scope: Dual-model Qwen3-VL sparse physical-observation proposals on the complete 27.5-second candidate
summary: Qwen3-VL-4B and 8B produced hash-bound long-span contact and flower-motion hypotheses, but their low agreement rejects either model as physical truth.
evidence: Both models processed the same 14 uniformly spaced frames from candidate SHA-256 bf15763ff5ceeb26bd2a744045d76579bad2b758ffa787176e4e8693d5a5ff91 on separate physical A800 GPUs.
Qwen3-VL-4B inference took 63.914578 seconds at 0.219042 sampled FPS with 9417.804 MiB peak allocated memory.
Qwen3-VL-8B inference took 62.401663 seconds at 0.224353 sampled FPS with 17820.477 MiB peak allocated memory.
Four-field categorical agreement is 0.285714; 4B labels flower motion after 2.125 seconds while 8B labels contact with a static flower at all 14 samples.
Both reports explicitly mark metric depth, absolute scale, full q/qdot, contact force, and force closure as non-observable.
lessons: Different sizes of one VLM family can produce mutually incompatible physical narratives from identical sparse pixels.
VLM output is useful for failure-window mining only when a deterministic authority layer prevents it from becoming a measurement.
limitations: The 14 full-frame samples are too sparse and low resolution to accept finger integrity or continuous flower motion.
Neither model adds a physical acquisition group, metric scale, hidden joint state, or force observation.
next_actions: Use model disagreement to target continuous real RGB-D/extra-camera capture and synchronized q/qdot rather than generating more pseudo sensors.
